en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
7. The Second Mansion of the Ship “O woman,
you stand having boarded a ship with a golden canopy.”
"You have entered the lotus pond and are plucking the lotuses with your hand.
By what means do you possess such a complexion?"
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those riches that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she gave an answer as the fruit of that very deed:
"When I was among humans, having become a human being..."
In a previous birth in the human world,
having seen a thirsty and weary bhikkhu,
I rose up and gave him water to drink.
Whoever gives water to drink to one who is weary and thirsty after rising,
for him there shall be rivers of cool water.
Abounding with many garlands and many white lotuses,
that river flows around it at all times—
a river of cool water, strewn with sands.
Amba trees, salas, and tilakas, jambus,
uddālakas, and pāṭalis were in full bloom;
that place was endowed with such grounds.
This most excellent celestial mansion shines with great splendor;
this is the fruition here of that very deed—
those who have performed merit obtain such as this.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this;
because of that, I prosper here;
and wealth arises for me.
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
O monk of great power, I declare to you—
that those who were human beings performed meritorious deeds."
"Thus I possess such blazing power,
and my radiance illuminates all directions.
The second ship-vimāna, the seventh.
